title: Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators
digest_headline: Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators: a lynx starts hunting kites
summary: Disease crashed the shared prey (rabbits). After decades of neutral co-existence, lynx then began preying heavily on kites, a top raptor.
caveats: One long-term system. The owl increase is an association, not a tested cascade. Check the paper for species and site details.

title: OCTRON - a general purpose segmentation and tracking pipeline for behavioral experiments
digest_headline: OCTRON: foundation-model masks → compact segmentation/detection models → multi-object tracks, with a napari curation UI
summary: OCTRON swaps sparse skeletons for full-body masks, which suit deformable animals better. Segmentation foundation models generate annotations from minimal input.
caveats: Preprint, and the abstract gives no tracking metrics (IDF1, HOTA). The tests are lab setups, not free-swimming reef video.

title: β-Stability: Efficient, human-in-the-loop, graph-based curation of individual animal identities from images
digest_headline: β-Stability: human-in-the-loop, graph-based curation of individual animal IDs (bioRxiv, 20 Oct)
summary: Nepovinnykh, Haucke, … Beery, Stewart et al. Re-ID matches (MiewID) become a graph, and a stability measure sends the expert only to the edges that matter.

title: Optimizing sampling and monitoring of species interactions within Biodiversity Observation Networks
digest_headline: Monitoring species interactions needs far more sampling than monitoring species, but a known species range gets you a long way
summary: Simulations of Biodiversity Observation Networks show the sampling effort needed is considerably higher for interactions than for species, especially when realising and detecting an interaction depends on abundance. The good news: for a focal species, placing sites using its known range recovered its interactions efficiently.
caveats: Simulation only. Automated pipelines add classifier error on top of the sampling problem.

title: MarineLife-16K: An Attribute-Rich Video-Text Dataset for Motion-Aware Marine Video Understanding
digest_headline: MarineLife-16K: a video-text benchmark for marine video understanding (arXiv, 24 Oct)
summary: 2,000 in-the-wild marine video-text pairs from 7 countries, annotated with 13 attributes (objects, behaviours, environment, camera motion), giving 16,080 video-question pairs. Benchmarked video-LLMs handle object motion well but struggle with complex camera motion and with reasoning in static-camera footage.

title: A million orthopteran singers from a year of continuously operating field recorders detected, tracked and organized by song
digest_headline: A million orthopteran singers: unsupervised detection, tracking and cataloguing of insect song from 175,896 recorder-hours
summary: Insect choruses lack discrete calls and labelled libraries, so this method exploits repetitive song instead. It separates singers in minute windows, links them across a night as frequency and syllable rate drift with temperature, and builds a catalogue across days and sites.
caveats: Single-author preprint from one site. It relies on repetitive song, so it won't transfer directly to irregular reef-fish sounds. Song types aren't species yet.

title: A Perch out of Water: Few-Shot Detection of Bryde's Whale Vocalisations in False Bay
digest_headline: A Perch out of water: few-shot whale call detection with bird-trained embeddings (arXiv, 21 Oct)
summary: With ≤10 examples per call type and no fine-tuning, retuning Perch's input (longer frames, mel range restricted to the calls) and per-call detection gained 9.1 AUC points (macro AUC 0.739, Antarctic blue/fin whales). On Bryde's whales in False Bay, Perch beat the whale-specific WhaleVAD for every call type.

title: Sound advice: A calibration framework for defining detection space in passive acoustic monitoring
digest_headline: Sound advice: calibrating the “detection space” of acoustic recorders (PLOS One, 27 Oct)
summary: Pure-tone playbacks (1–8 kHz) over 50–300 m in the Western Ghats found 1 kHz signals dropped to 50% detection at about 100 m, while 4–6 kHz stayed reliable to 250 m. Recorder orientation mattered hugely: 81% detection facing the source versus 14% rear-facing.

title: From Risk to Application: What Critically Endangered means for the world's coral reefs
digest_headline: First global Red List of Ecosystems assessment for coral reefs: 122 of 127 ecoregions Critically Endangered
summary: The first global Red List of Ecosystems assessment of reefs puts 122 of 127 ecoregions at extremely high risk of collapse within 50 years, including ecoregions that still look healthy. The main driver is marine-heatwave frequency, which exceeds tolerable limits even under the moderate SSP2-4.5 scenario.
caveats: Preprint. Risk is driven by projected heatwaves more than observed collapse, so check the regional report for any system you cite.

title: Marine heat waves in vulnerable coral reef regions are skillfully predictable on multi-year timescales
digest_headline: Marine heatwaves on vulnerable reefs are predictable years ahead (Nature Communications, 27 Oct)
summary: Karwat, Lee, Franzke et al. used CESM2 five-year hindcasts (1981–2020) across 12 reef regions. Heatwave frequency and cumulative intensity are predictable months to multiple years ahead in many basins, mostly thanks to anthropogenic warming.

title: Changing coral disease dynamics with the emergence of stony coral tissue loss disease on reefs at Carrie Bow Cay, Belize Barrier Reef
digest_headline: SCTLD arrives on the Belize Barrier Reef (Frontiers in Marine Science, 20 Oct)
summary: Nine Carrie Bow Cay sites surveyed from 2019 to 2024. Disease prevalence rose from 0.5% to 6.2% by 2022.

title: BioCluster: Clustering and Zero-Shot Labeling of Ecological Images Using Foundation Models
digest_headline: BioCluster: species labels for camera-trap images with zero task-specific training
summary: BioCluster takes pretrained foundation-model embeddings, clusters images into taxonomic groups without training, then names clusters by zero-shot text matching against the expected taxa. A per-image uncertainty score sorts images into three confidence tiers so experts only review the hard ones.
caveats: Preprint, tested on moths and birds. Turbid, blue-shifted reef imagery is a bigger domain shift, and you need a candidate species list.

title: Weakly Supervised Fish Segmentation through Point-Supervised Tracking and Motion-Informed Language
digest_headline: One click per fish: weakly supervised fish segmentation (arXiv, 21 Oct)
summary: A point tracker propagates single clicks, those points become “motion-informed language” prompts for a segmentation model, and optical flow cleans up the result. Full masks can take up to 2 min per fish to draw by hand.

title: Eyes in the Wild and Minds in the Loop: A Systematic Review of Artificial Intelligence for Camera-Trap Wildlife Monitoring
digest_headline: AI for camera traps, systematically reviewed: behaviour recognition appears in only 5% of 201 studies
summary: A PRISMA 2020 review of 201 studies (2020–2026). Output grows about 29% a year.
caveats: Single-author review of Scopus journal articles, so conference papers (where much behaviour CV lives) are excluded. Terrestrial camera traps only.

title: Field testing the influence of settlement recesses and nighttime feeding lights on coral recruitment
digest_headline: Settlement recesses and night-time feeding lights for coral recruitment (Scientific Reports, 22 Oct)
summary: Jorissen, Reichert, Dixon & Madin ran a 6-month test on concrete restoration modules in Kāneʻohe Bay. Recesses dramatically improved initial larval entrainment, and survival at 6 months was higher in deeper recesses.

title: Performance of Acropora species on the Great Barrier Reef's first coral tree nursery
digest_headline: The GBR's first coral tree nursery: 10 Acropora species after 6 months (Restoration Ecology, 20 Oct)
summary: Kish, Carter, Settli, Saparwan et al. Nursery fragments grew faster, with less predation and disease than wild controls, and harvesting did not harm donor colonies.

title: Safeguarding global terrestrial vertebrate species from future sea level rise
digest_headline: Sea level rise and 34,120 terrestrial vertebrates (Science, 22 Oct)
summary: Jiang, Xiao, Hanson, Zeng et al. Exposed species rise from up to 13,680 in 2050 to 15,324 by 2100, including 57–63% of birds.

title: Spatial reorganization during post-collapse population growth suggests conspecific attraction in baleen whale nursing grounds
digest_headline: Recovering whales cluster together: conspecific attraction in southern right whale nursing grounds (PNAS, 26 Oct)
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: 47 years of Australian aerial surveys (1976–2023). As numbers grew from a few individuals to a few hundred, distributions shifted from dispersed to clustered, and site fidelity was weaker than assumed.
venue_clean: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

title: WildDepth-v2: A Synchronized RGB--LiDAR--Radar Dataset and Benchmark for Metric Depth, Motion, and Tracking of Wildlife
digest_headline: WildDepth-v2: synchronised RGB–LiDAR–radar wildlife dataset (arXiv, 22 Oct)
summary: 37 sequences with 4D imaging radar (to the authors' knowledge, the first wildlife radar recordings), plus a hidden test set for depth. Once-per-track radar scaling cut 3D position error four-fold (2.20 to 0.58 m) and distance-sampling bias from −13% to −2%.

title: MarineSet: Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Data Curation and evaluation
digest_headline: MarineSet: 3,000 curated hours from 41 years of NOAA hydrophone audio (arXiv, 21 Oct)
summary: A scalable curation pipeline builds a diverse self-supervised pretraining set. The baseline MarineNet is competitive on marine-mammal call and ship-type classification.

title: Listening to the City: Evaluating BirdNET Reliability and Bias in Urban Bird Community Assessments
digest_headline: BirdNET in the city: more than half the detected “species” weren't there
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
summary: About 723 h of audio from Turin and Florence, with up to 500 detections per species checked by hand. BirdNET reported 192 and 203 species; only 48 and 65 were confirmed, so 58% and 52% of detected species were false.
caveats: Off-the-shelf urban bird model, not reefs. Decent segment precision can coexist with badly inflated species lists.
venue_clean: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation

title: Do bioacoustic foundation models hear through the noise ? SNR and generalization in underwater detection
digest_headline: Do bioacoustic foundation models hear through the noise? Mostly no (arXiv, 20 Oct)
summary: Four frozen encoders were tested on continuous Kerguelen Plateau recordings. Evaluation SNR explained more variation in average precision than model choice, performance peaked only when train and test noise matched, and AP stayed low throughout.

title: Hydromorphological Restoration of Streams Does Not Ensure the Recovery of Ecosystem Functioning
digest_headline: Null of the week: restoring stream habitat doesn't restore ecosystem function (Global Change Biology, 22 Oct)
summary: Haase et al. pooled 582 effect sizes from 66 studies. Gross primary production was higher in degraded than reference streams, denitrification was lower in restored than degraded ones, and restoration didn't consistently reverse functional differences.

title: Dispersal corridors enhance modelled near-bed larval connectivity across deep-sea protected area networks
digest_headline: Deep-sea mining: protected areas in the Clarion–Clipperton Zone barely connect (Nature Ecology & Evolution, 23 Oct)
summary: James, Bridges, Jones, Clubley et al. found fewer than 0.02% of modelled larvae reach another protected area (APEI) under realistic near-bed dispersal of 19–69 days. Strategic corridors increased inter-APEI dispersal 406-fold.

title: Conflict with industrial fleets undermines the contributions of small-scale fisheries to sustainable development in vulnerable regions
digest_headline: Industrial fleets vs small-scale fisheries in 126 countries (Nature Food, 22 Oct)
summary: Cronin, Finkbeiner, Virdin et al. built a conflict-interaction index. Vulnerability peaks where small-scale fisheries are vital for nutrition but governance is weak (especially Africa, Oceania and Asia).

title: BES Annual Meeting 2026, ICC Birmingham, 14–17 Dec 2026
digest_headline: BES Annual Meeting 2026, ICC Birmingham, 14–17 Dec 2026
summary: Earlybird registration closes 17:00 GMT on Tue 3 Nov (presenters must register by then to keep their slot). Virtual tickets are on sale until 17:00 GMT on Fri 13 Nov.

title: CVPR 2027: workshops on 20–21 June 2027 in Seattle
digest_headline: CVPR 2027: workshops on 20–21 June 2027 in Seattle
summary: Workshop proposals are due 4 Nov 2026 AoE. No CV4Animals 2027 call has been published yet (the 2026 edition ran on 4 June in Denver).

title: FSBI Travel Grant: next closing date 1 Dec 2026, 23:59 GMT
digest_headline: FSBI Travel Grant: next closing date 1 Dec 2026, 23:59 GMT
summary: Up to £1,500, FSBI members only, applied for 3–12 months before travel. Good for a 2027 conference trip. fsbi.org.uk

title: FSBI Small Research Grant: next closing date 5 Jan 2027
digest_headline: FSBI Small Research Grant: next closing date 5 Jan 2027
summary: Up to £10,000 for fish biology research. Check eligibility and scope on the page before planning a bid. fsbi.org.uk

title: Company of Biologists Travelling Fellowships: next deadline 5 Feb 2027
digest_headline: Company of Biologists Travelling Fellowships: next deadline 5 Feb 2027
summary: Up to £3,000 for a research visit to another lab. The Journal of Experimental Biology scheme is the natural fit for behaviour work.

title: BES grants 2027: dates “confirmed in early December”
digest_headline: BES grants 2027: dates “confirmed in early December”
summary: In 2026 the Training and Travel rounds closed on 25 Jan, 17 May and 8 Sep (up to £500 for PhD students). The 2027 dates aren't published yet.

title: Who Called? V33DA: A Physically Verified Multimodal Benchmark for Vocal Attribution in Zebra Finch Groups
digest_headline: Who called? V33DA: a physically verified multimodal benchmark for working out which bird in a group vocalised
summary: Attributing a call to an individual in a group is the core of social-communication research, but it is rarely tested against physical ground truth. V33DA has 33,625 verified events from social zebra finches (10 birds, three experiments).
caveats: Preprint. Captive zebra finches in an instrumented arena, not a reef. The abstract reports the gap qualitatively, so check the paper for accuracies.

title: Recruitment pulses cause a market dilemma in cleaning interactions from a tropical Atlantic rocky reef
digest_headline: Recruitment pulses create a “market dilemma” in a cleaning network (Behavioral Ecology, 31 Oct)
summary: Garcia, Suhett, Lessa, Mello-Fonseca, Quimbayo & Dias followed cleaning interactions on a rocky reef at Arraial do Cabo (SW Atlantic) for three years. The dedicated cleaner goby Elacatinus figaro was the most important cleaner in the network despite low abundance.

title: Beggars can't be choosers: Competitive dominance and size‐dependent resource investment jointly constrain partner associations in a multispecies mutualism
digest_headline: Beggars can't be choosers: who gets the best aphids (Journal of Animal Ecology, 28 Oct)
summary: Nelson, Nguyen, Levings, Hawk & Mooney combined sugar baits with censuses of wild aphid colonies. The dominant ant recruited to bigger baits and monopolised the largest colonies.

title: From pose to behavior: SABER integrates identity-resolved multi-animal pose tracking with large-language-model-based behavioral factor discovery
digest_headline: SABER: identity-resolved multi-animal pose plus LLM-mined behavioural features (bioRxiv, 26 Oct)
summary: Zheng, Peng, Zhang et al. couple multi-animal pose estimation with identity-preserving tracking, then mine interpretable kinematic, postural and social descriptors and classify behaviour over multiple timescales from one overhead camera. It beat comparator pipelines on pose accuracy and tracking continuity across social, mating and aggression recordings in mice.

title: A Scalable Workflow for Extracting Species Interactions From Ecological Literature Using Large Language Models
digest_headline: An LLM workflow pulls 144,402 species interactions from 83,910 papers, at 89.5% precision
summary: A replicable workflow uses GPT-4o to extract a broad range of biological interactions (not just feeding) directly from the literature. Run on 83,910 articles, it produced a network of 144,402 interactions among 36,471 taxa.
caveats: Recall of 70% means roughly 3 in 10 reported interactions are missed. Literature bias (well-studied taxa and regions) carries straight into the network. It relies on a proprietary model.

title: Overexploitation risks disproportionate vertebrate downsizing and declines in potential dispersal distances in frugivory networks
digest_headline: Overexploitation strips the big frugivores out of seed-dispersal networks (Proc B, 28 Oct)
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
summary: Morton, Lurgi & Edwards simulated losing overexploited species from 160 frugivory networks (>16,000 interactions). Body-mass downsizing was six-fold greater than under random loss.
venue_clean: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

title: A richness-sensitive Acoustic Biodiversity Index from species-level detections: classifier benchmarking, false-positive control and validation against standard soundscape indices in an African savanna and an urban zoo
digest_headline: A species-level Acoustic Biodiversity Index tracks richness (ρ = 0.93) where standard soundscape indices don't
summary: Classic acoustic indices summarise sound energy, not species. This ABI is Shannon diversity of species-level detections, normalised by the regional species pool expected for the site and season.
caveats: Preprint, birds only, two sites. The index inherits classifier errors, so it depends on a good regional species list and false-positive control.

title: 4-Dimensional Chess: Acoustic Localisation Reveals Nested Spatio-temporal Strategies in an Arboreal Communication Network
digest_headline: 4-dimensional chess: 3D acoustic localisation of a reed-frog chorus (bioRxiv, 28 Oct)
summary: Basham, Larter, Champagne, Jones & Keitt tracked individual male Hyperolius sp. A in a wild rainforest chorus using 3D acoustic localisation and source separation.

title: Pygmy blue whale feeding drives greater nocturnal than diurnal song production
digest_headline: Pygmy blue whales sing more at night because they're busy eating by day (R Soc Open Sci, 28 Oct)
summary: Davenport, Thums, Jenner et al. combined PAM with 130.1 days of dive data. Diurnal feeding left less time for singing, so a night-heavy song ratio could act as an acoustic indicator of population-level feeding.

title: Deep learning reveals persistent individual signatures in bat echolocation calls of the greater leaf-nosed bat
digest_headline: CNNs find individual signatures in bat echolocation calls (Zoological Research, 1 Nov)
summary: Li, Huang, Xie et al. recorded 17,584 calls from 34 greater leaf-nosed bats. A CNN identified individuals at 84% (single calls) and 91% (sequences), against 39% and 47% for discriminant function analysis.

title: Delayed bleaching-induced coral mortality limits reef recovery after a marine heatwave
digest_headline: Delayed bleaching mortality: on Mo’orea, coral cover kept falling for four years after the 2019 heatwave
summary: Two long-term datasets cover 13 sites after Mo’orea's most severe recorded heatwave, where peak accumulated heat stress ranged 5.76–6.26 °C-weeks. Pocillopora mortality rose with heat stress and mean cover collapsed from 35% to 17% within a year.
caveats: Preprint, one island. Delayed mortality could partly reflect other stressors in later years. Check the paper for how these were handled.

title: Corallivore impacts on corals under ocean warming depend on both consumer and prey responses to rising temperatures
digest_headline: Warming makes corallivores more damaging, in two different ways (MEPS, 29 Oct)
summary: Altman-Kurosaki & Hay paired two corallivorous snails with two corals. Warming raised Drupella cornus respiration about 1.5× and shifted it onto its less-preferred coral.

title: Cumulative thermal stress predicts functional change in coral reef fish communities
digest_headline: Heat stress reshapes reef fish functional composition across northern Australia (Proc B, 28 Oct)
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
summary: Markey, Fordham, Stuart-Smith, Edgar, Brown & Mellin fitted a Bayesian joint species distribution model to 500 species at 286 sites. Along the heatwave gradient they predict losses of habitat specialists, large-bodied fish, corallivores and pelagic feeders. doi:10.1098/rspb.2026.1955
venue_clean: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

title: Global Change Is Reshaping Coral Communities and Threatening Reef Physical Functionality
digest_headline: Coral cover isn't reef function (Global Change Biology, 29 Oct)
summary: Álvarez-Filip reviews how global change removes dominant, architecturally complex corals first. Cover can rebound with fast-growing opportunists while reef framework and complexity lag by decades.

title: Dreams Are Cheaper Than Flights: Curated World-Model Data Improves Aerial Detection
digest_headline: Dreams are cheaper than flights: world-model video improves wildlife drone detectors
summary: A 7B-parameter video world model was seeded with real wildlife drone frames and asked to extend each scene into new footage with the same sensor, altitude and environment. Curated frames more than doubled the training set.
caveats: Preprint. Tested on the same drones and sites (not new ones). Expert curation is still the hidden cost. Whether this works for underwater video and fine-grained behaviour is untested.

title: AquaProbe: Efficient Adaptation of Frozen Vision Models for Underwater Images
digest_headline: AquaProbe: put your LoRA budget where the underwater domain gap is (arXiv, 29 Oct)
summary: Shovo, Paul, Dong & Lin measure where in a frozen encoder the underwater gap appears (it shifts with water type and range), then allocate LoRA ranks to match. With the same 0.59M adapter parameters, proportional allocation reached 70.1 mIoU, 1.9 points above uniform.

title: FieldGuideRAG: Image-Grounded GraphRAG for Fine-Grained Recognition with Vision-Language Models
digest_headline: FieldGuideRAG: a VLM checks your photo against a photo on every species node (arXiv, 29 Oct)
summary: Training-free. A knowledge graph stores one real photo per species plus range and ecological facts.

title: Detection of trade in products derived from threatened species using machine learning and a smartphone application
digest_headline: Spotting pangolin, tiger and elephant products in online images (Conservation Biology, 26 Oct)
summary: Kulkarni, Wu & Di Minin trained Faster R-CNN on 39,941 images that include look-alike non-wildlife items. Overall accuracy was 84.2% (pangolin 93.6%, tiger 90.3%, elephant 71.1%).

title: From deployment to functioning ecosystems: assessing taxonomic richness and community composition on modular shellfish reefs using environmental DNA metabarcoding
digest_headline: Modular shellfish reefs: richness comes fast, the community keeps changing (bioRxiv, 29 Oct)
summary: Tettamanti, Staples, Mos, Porter, Gilby & Cheney used eDNA on reefs aged 9, 21 and 42 months. Genus richness rose quickly, but composition kept shifting and converged with age, a change invisible to richness alone.

title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
digest_headline: A global map of 45 threats to 21,490 freshwater species (Science, 29 Oct)
summary: Brabant, Pollock, Geldmann, Bendixen, Comte & Farooq. Species in highly developed, water-managed regions face multiple overlapping threats, and freshwater species face greater threat intensity than terrestrial ones.

title: Resource-driven release from lag phase triggers the world’s fastest and largest coastal plant invasion
digest_headline: Why invasions wait, then explode: sediment ends Spartina's lag phase (PNAS, 26 Oct)
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Ge, Richardson, Pyšek, Cai & Chen. Experiments, models and historical records suggest sediment supply weakens Allee effects in Spartina alterniflora, so the lag phase depends on resources, not fixed species traits. doi:10.1073/pnas.2622290123
venue_clean: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

title: Nereus: A Large-Scale Underwater Dataset for Fine-Grained Attribute Understanding and Grounded Counting Perception
digest_headline: Nereus: 88K underwater images, 2.68M question-answer pairs, 2,690 species (arXiv, 30 Oct)
summary: 136K annotated organisms across 1,515 genera, plus 65K point annotations and 67K grounded counting questions. Training on it improved multimodal models' downstream adaptation over existing underwater data.

title: Open-set multi-view seahorse re-identification from underwater photograph sequences
digest_headline: Open-set seahorse re-ID from photo sequences (arXiv, 29 Oct)
summary: Fauvel, Louisy, Louisy & Fauvel: 35,914 wild photos of 474 individual seahorses. Combining several photos per encounter gives state-of-the-art re-ID, plus taxon and sex classification.

title: Taxonomy‐informed hierarchical deep learning for otolith image identification in coral reef fishes
digest_headline: Taxonomy-aware deep learning for coral reef fish otoliths (Journal of Fish Biology, 29 Oct)
summary: Kang, Wang, Liu et al. built taxonomic constraints into the model. Species accuracy rose from 94.80% to 98.00%, with far fewer cross-family mistakes, and it handled 33 unseen species from a few examples.

title: A common marking method influences fish-parasite interactions
digest_headline: Marking isn't neutral: elastomer-tagged guppies carried about 3.7× more parasites
summary: Visible Implant Elastomer (VIE) tags are a standard way to tell fish apart, and earlier studies found no effect on survival, growth or behaviour. This study compared 26 VIE-marked with 46 control guppies.
caveats: Single-author preprint, one host-parasite system, modest sample sizes.

title: Every scientist a modeller? The promise and peril of AI ‐assisted mechanistic models
digest_headline: Every scientist a modeller? The promise and peril of AI-assisted mechanistic models (MEE, 26 Oct)
summary: Sen Gupta works through a predator–prey model built with AI and shows where decisions get quietly delegated: hidden assumptions, and plausible but wrong code. The fixes are practical.

title: CBD COP17 closes in Yerevan with the “Yerevan Pathway” (31 Oct)
digest_headline: CBD COP17 closes in Yerevan with the “Yerevan Pathway” (31 Oct)
summary: The first global review found the world off track on the Kunming-Montreal framework's 23 targets for 2030. Nearly 50 decisions were adopted, including on marine and coastal biodiversity, with nearly US$2bn in new funding announcements and rules (the “Sevan Guidelines”) for the new Article 8(j) body on Indigenous peoples and local communities.

title: Fiji gets US$35.2m from the Green Climate Fund for the Great Sea Reef (29 Oct)
digest_headline: Fiji gets US$35.2m from the Green Climate Fund for the Great Sea Reef (29 Oct)
summary: Part of a US$42.6m ridge-to-reef project: more than 3,000 ha of mangrove and riparian restoration, climate-resilient management over 2.58 million ha of reef, and a locally led adaptation fund. PINA

title: Pemba's community co-managed MPAs, 1,300 km² of reef, mangrove and seagrass (Mongabay, 29 Oct)
digest_headline: Pemba's community co-managed MPAs, 1,300 km² of reef, mangrove and seagrass (Mongabay, 29 Oct)
summary: Two new conservation areas off Pemba (Zanzibar, Tanzania) were gazetted in June 2026 after work with more than 20 communities. Blue Alliance reports patrols up more than 50% and illegal activity down about 45%.

title: African Bioacoustics Community conference (21–27 Nov) and Mpala workshop (29 Nov–4 Dec), Kenya
digest_headline: African Bioacoustics Community conference (21–27 Nov) and Mpala workshop (29 Nov–4 Dec), Kenya
summary: The organisers list the conference at Lake Naivasha as hybrid, with online presentation possible (abstracts have closed). The residential Little Bioacoustics Jamii workshop at Mpala covers data collection, big datasets and ML for automated detection. africanbioacoustics.org · Mpala workshop

title: ASAB/PSGB Winter Meeting: social learning and culture, Edinburgh, 8–10 Dec
digest_headline: ASAB/PSGB Winter Meeting: social learning and culture, Edinburgh, 8–10 Dec
summary: The ASAB days (8–9 Dec) can be attended online. The PSGB day (10 Dec) costs £35–£100.

title: Coming up: UN climate summit COP31, Antalya, 9–20 Nov
digest_headline: Coming up: UN climate summit COP31, Antalya, 9–20 Nov
summary: It follows straight on from the biodiversity COP. Worth watching for ocean and coastal-resilience outcomes.

title: Challenger Society Travel Awards: next deadline 15 Jan 2027
digest_headline: Challenger Society Travel Awards: next deadline 15 Jan 2027
summary: For student members at UK institutions: £250 (UK) or £500 (international) for conferences, cruises or fieldwork. PhD students can receive two awards.

title: MBA Student Travel Bursary: round 2 runs 5 Jan–16 Feb 2027
digest_headline: MBA Student Travel Bursary: round 2 runs 5 Jan–16 Feb 2027
summary: Student/Postgraduate MBA members only, with a supervisor letter. Each round gives one award of up to £500 and two of up to £250.

title: One for later: ASAB Research Grants (next deadline 1 Feb 2027)
digest_headline: One for later: ASAB Research Grants (next deadline 1 Feb 2027)
summary: Up to £10,000 (£15,000 with justification) for pilot behaviour projects. You need a PhD and 12 months' membership, and it won't fund thesis work, so this is postdoc planning.

title: Automated identification of individual birds by song enables multi-year recapture from passive acoustic monitoring data
digest_headline: Recapture without the capture: 405 ovenbirds identified from their songs alone, across four years
summary: Camera traps and recorders usually stop at species. Tracking individuals still means capture-mark-recapture.
caveats: One species with a stereotyped, individually distinctive song, and territorial males that stay put. Species with variable or shared repertoires, or that move a lot, will be harder. Clustering errors (one bird split in two, or two merged) feed straight into survival estimates, so check the paper's error analysis before you borrow the numbers.

title: The repeated evolution of anti-bat bioacoustics in hawkmoths
digest_headline: Hawkmoths evolved ultrasonic anti-bat sounds again and again (Proc R Soc B, 4 Nov)
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
summary: Masonick, Petricic, Giusti, Couch, Barber & Kawahara combined acoustic recordings, electron microscopy, micro-CT and a time-calibrated phylogeny. They describe three stridulatory systems (scale-on-scale, scale-on-spine, scale-on-nodule).
venue_clean: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

title: HMMF-Net: A Lightweight Hierarchical Multi-Frame Multimodal Fusion Network for Accurate Fish Feeding Intensity Assessment
digest_headline: HMMF-Net: audio plus video for fish feeding intensity, small enough for a Jetson (arXiv, 6 Nov)
summary: Hoang, Tran, Trinh & Phan fuse stacked video frames with log-mel spectrograms through compact “messenger tokens” rather than heavy cross-attention. On the AV-FFIA dataset: 96.77% accuracy with 3.99M parameters, cutting classification error by 28% against the best video-only setup, and 11.5 ms per 2-s clip on a Jetson Orin Nano.

title: Towards ecologically meaningful foundation models
digest_headline: A roadmap for ecological foundation models that actually encode ecology
summary: The authors argue that ecological foundation models (ecoFMs) should be trained on large multimodal ecological datasets and informed by ecological theory. The goal is shared representations of organisms, environments and interactions, which could improve generalisation and link pattern to process.
caveats: A perspective, so no new results. “Theory-guided” foundation models are mostly an aspiration so far, and evaluation is the hard part.

title: The environmental dependence of ecological interaction networks
digest_headline: Goodbye, deterministic metaweb? Interactions depend on the environment (Biological Reviews, 2 Nov)
summary: Parisy, Cirtwill & Roslin use simulations and empirical networks to show that both species occurrence and link occurrence are stochastic, with probabilities conditional on the environment. They argue for dropping the assumption that two co-occurring species always interact.

title: Drowning in Noise: On Signal Saliency in Self-Supervised Learning for Ocean Acoustics
digest_headline: Drowning in noise: 30 hours of curated whale audio beat 1,240 hours of everything
summary: Self-supervised audio models usually improve with more pre-training data. But passive ocean recordings are mostly waves, wind and silence, with vocalisations a tiny fraction.
caveats: Preprint, one SSL model family and one downstream benchmark. Manual curation is itself labour, and the automatic filter isn't there yet.

title: NAVE: A Normalized, Adaptive Conformer for Antarctic Whale Vocalization Detection
digest_headline: NAVE: a noise-aware Conformer for Antarctic whale calls (arXiv, 6 Nov)
summary: Nagl, Primus & Widmer suppress site-specific background with per-bin mean subtraction plus a PCEN channel, and match the convolution kernel to call duration. On BioDCASE 2026 Task 2, with leave-one-site-out validation (a proxy for new deployments), one model beat the stronger WhaleVAD-BPN baseline.

title: Detecting whale vocalizations up to 2.5 kHz using a seafloor distributed acoustic sensing array with incorporated loops
digest_headline: Looped fibre-optic cable hears killer whales up to 2.5 kHz (JASA, 2 Nov)
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
summary: Juber, Brandicourt, Veirs, Veirs, Lipovsky & Abadi added loops to a seafloor distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) cable in Haro Strait. Looped sections recorded up to 2.5 kHz versus about 500 Hz for straight ones, picking up Southern Resident and Bigg's killer whales and humpbacks.
venue_clean: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America

title: Marine Heatwave and Extreme Hypoxia Coincide With Rapid Coral Bleaching and Mortality on a Central Red Sea Coral Reef
digest_headline: Not just heat: a Red Sea reef bleached and died within days as night-time oxygen crashed
summary: In mid-2024 a severe marine heatwave hit a central Red Sea reef, and it coincided with repeated night-time low-oxygen events. As water passed 33°C, night oxygen minima fell to 15.2–57.8 µmol O₂ kg⁻¹, and the day-night temperature swing shrank to 0.31–0.67°C, so there was no cool reprieve at night.
caveats: One reef and one event, with an observational design. The authors show the conditions coincided, but don't experimentally separate heat from hypoxia.

title: Automated Coral Detection and Instance Segmentation in Underwater Imagery: Evaluating YOLO Model Performance and Transferability to Mesophotic Coral Ecosystems
digest_headline: YOLO instance segmentation for 57 Caribbean coral species, with a mesophotic transfer test (JMSE, 5 Nov)
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
summary: Cordero, Sherman, Bayo Torres, Raju & Yadav trained on 9,500+ hand-annotated images. YOLOv9e reached mask mAP₅₀ 0.789 for species and 0.870 for genus, at about 5 ms per image.
venue_clean: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

title: Influence of soft coral density and depth on benthic communities on Fiji's Rainbow Reef
digest_headline: Soft corals and benthic associations on Fiji's Rainbow Reef (R Soc Open Sci, 4 Nov)
summary: Stephenson … Mitchell & Manica combined Bayesian network inference with spatial point-process analysis. Depth dominated, and white Nephtheidae soft corals were negatively associated with stony corals and positively with algae.

title: How Finely Can Vision-Language Models See Biology? Bio-VQA: A Benchmark for Taxonomic, Morphological, Spatial and Individual Reasoning
digest_headline: Bio-VQA: 18 vision-language models can't reliably count, measure or re-identify animals
summary: A benchmark of 1.86M questions over 217K images from 11 public datasets, covering taxonomy, traits, counting and individual re-identification. It uses graded scoring, so a near-miss scores better than a wild guess.
caveats: Preprint. Open-weight models only, so no GPT-class or Gemini-class systems. Adversarial re-ID is a deliberately hard setting.

title: How many labels do you need? A decision framework for cross‐habitat marine biodiversity monitoring
digest_headline: How many labels do you need? 10–20 per class, if you stay in the same habitat (Ecol Solutions & Evidence, 6 Nov)
summary: Saleh & Rahimi Azghadi ran 900+ transfer experiments across reefs (GBR, French Polynesia) and a Danish fjord. Frozen DINOv2 + a linear classifier (1,538 trainable parameters) generalised to unseen reef sites at least as well as fully fine-tuned CNNs four orders of magnitude larger.

title: FishSense Lite: A Camera-Based, Single Laser Hardware Framework with Software System for In Situ Fish Length Measurement
digest_headline: FishSense Lite: fish lengths from one photo, a dive laser and a 3D-printed mount (arXiv, 5 Nov)
summary: Crutchfield … Semmens & Schurgers turn the laser dot's position into range, and range into length. Against stereo video on 7 wild fish, there was no detectable bias (+0.8%).

section: Climate, human impacts and ecosystem services
title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat
digest_headline: Noise pollution altered traits in 80% of species studied, and disrupted predator–prey interactions
summary: Phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species, with ranges spanning six continents. Anthropogenic noise altered at least one physiological, developmental or behavioural trait in 80% of species.
caveats: Experimental studies, often short-term exposures, so scaling to chronic real-world noise needs care. A meta-analysis is only as good as its literature (publication bias, uneven taxa).

section: Climate, human impacts and ecosystem services
title: Long-term impacts of deep-sea mining on sediment organic matter quantity and quality
digest_headline: A 1979 deep-sea mining test still shows 44 years later (Elementa, 2 Nov)
summary: Jeffreys and colleagues (SMARTEX) sampled a 1979 nodule-mining test site in the Clarion-Clipperton Zone at about 4,800 m. They found lower quantity and quality of sediment organic matter than at an undisturbed control site, linked to the lower animal abundances seen in SMARTEX imagery. doi:10.1525/elementa.2025.00106 · ON&T news

title: The potential of naturally stress‐tolerant corals to enhance reef recovery and restoration—A systematic review of transplantation studies from marginal and extreme reefs
digest_headline: “Tough” corals from extreme reefs don't automatically make better transplants (J Appl Ecol, 6 Nov)
summary: Zweifler, Sommer & Foo synthesised 306 transplantation measurements. Mesophotic-sourced corals grew better, but survival was mostly neutral (52.3%).

title: Five-year monitoring of coral nursery performance and reef-associated biodiversity at Pointe aux Feuilles, Mauritius, through the 2025 global bleaching event
digest_headline: Five years of coral nurseries in Mauritius, through the 2025 bleaching (Mar Pollut Bull, 7 Nov)
summary: Nazurally … Rinkevich report steady fragment survival in spider-frame and table nurseries. Crown-of-thorns numbers (39–62 a year) were strongly correlated with fish-trap presence.

title: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm
digest_headline: Common songbirds lost 43–49% of genomic diversity in a biodiversity hotspot (Science, 29 Oct)
summary: Liu, Liu, Wu, Yan & Dong compared historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, China. Common species were hit hardest, and many are still listed as Least Concern.

title: A strongly annotated passive acoustic dataset for tropical bird monitoring
digest_headline: PteroSet: strongly annotated Neotropical bird soundscapes (Scientific Data, 7 Nov)
summary: Ruiz, Ulloa, Miao … Lavista Ferres: 563 recordings (73.6 h) from two Colombian sites, with 15,372 time–frequency boxes, 6,702 of them to species (168 species). It uses COCO-style JSON, a binary detection baseline, and deliberately shows co-occurring calls and cross-site domain shift. doi:10.1038/s41597-026-08574-5

title: WhaleSonic: Recordings of cetacean vocal behaviour with hydrophone arrays in Northern Norway
digest_headline: WhaleSonic: synchronised hydrophone arrays on four whale species in a Norwegian fjord (bioRxiv, 3 Nov)
summary: Rychen … Hahnloser: four drifting tetrahedral-array buoys (78 h) plus seven bottom hydrophones (52 days), recorded while killer, humpback, fin and sperm whales shared a fjord in winter 2023–24. Recordings are time-synced and positioned to 2 m.

title: Snapshot Europe 2021–2022: The first public dataset from a Europe‐wide camera‐trap survey of terrestrial vertebrates
digest_headline: Snapshot Europe 2021–22: the first public Europe-wide camera-trap dataset (Ecology, 5 Nov)
summary: Iannarilli … Cagnacci and 160+ researchers: 90,230 camera-trap days across 22–23 countries, with 94,441 observations of 63 mammal species and 5,024 detections of 78 bird species. Every record was human-checked after AI classification, and the data are CC BY-SA 4.0. doi:10.1002/ecy.70516

title: Sparrow Model Zoo v0.33.0: conservation models packaged for edge inference (Zenodo, 6 Nov)
digest_headline: Sparrow Model Zoo v0.33.0: conservation models packaged for edge inference (Zenodo, 6 Nov)
summary: From Microsoft's AI for Good Lab and the Pytorch-Wildlife project: 80 active catalogue entries in ONNX and TFLite for the Sparrow Engine. They include camera-trap classifiers, HawkEars v2 and BatDetect2, and this release adds two overhead (drone) detectors.

title: Is conservation AI ready? Quantifying the challenges of automated species identification in Colombia
digest_headline: Is conservation AI ready? GPT-5.2 collapses on poorly photographed Colombian species
summary: The author tested GPT-5.2 on 10,000 research-grade iNaturalist images of Colombian vertebrates (amphibians, birds, fishes, mammals, reptiles), using localised prompts and no taxonomic metadata. Species-level accuracy scaled non-linearly with how well-photographed a species is globally, and decayed sharply for recently described taxa.
caveats: Single author, one proprietary model and one country. iNaturalist research-grade labels aren't perfect ground truth either.

title: COP31 opens today in Antalya (9–20 Nov)
digest_headline: COP31 opens today in Antalya (9–20 Nov)
summary: The UN climate summit follows straight on from the biodiversity COP, and it opens with an early fight over climate finance. Worth watching for ocean and coastal-resilience outcomes.

title: GOOS Status Report 2026: 67 countries, 17 networks, big gaps (5 Nov)
digest_headline: GOOS Status Report 2026: 67 countries, 17 networks, big gaps (5 Nov)
summary: The UNESCO-IOC report flags uneven, under-funded observing capacity concentrated among a few contributors. It names gaps in the Southern Ocean, polar regions, the deep ocean and many coasts, especially in developing countries and Small Island Developing States.

title: 6th Camera Traps, AI & Ecology workshop, Fribourg + online, 21–22 Jan 2027: papers due 27 Nov
digest_headline: 6th Camera Traps, AI & Ecology workshop, Fribourg + online, 21–22 Jan 2027: papers due 27 Nov
summary: Topics explicitly include video recognition of animal behaviour, tracking, re-ID and pose. Underwater and “other animal monitoring cameras” count too.

title: Royal Society of Biology Travel Grants: up to £1,000, close 22 Jan 2027
digest_headline: Royal Society of Biology Travel Grants: up to £1,000, close 22 Jan 2027
summary: Open to associate (AMRSB) and early-career MRSB members for future travel: fieldwork, lab visits, or overseas conferences (for MRSB, you must be presenting). Non-members can apply once they've submitted a paid membership application.

title: ECSA Charles Boyden Small Grants: £150–£500, next deadline 1 Feb 2027
digest_headline: ECSA Charles Boyden Small Grants: £150–£500, next deadline 1 Feb 2027
summary: For Estuarine & Coastal Sciences Association members who are postgrads or early-career researchers. It covers fieldwork, lab visits, conferences or training, needs a supervisor's recommendation and is paid in arrears.

title: Stony coral symbioses show variable responses to future ocean conditions
digest_headline: Coral symbioses under future oceans: adaptive in some species, random drift in others (Science Advances, 4 Nov)
summary: Rocha de Souza, Bruce, Cros, Jury, Drury & Toonen ran a 2.5-year factorial future-ocean mesocosm with eight coral species from the major lineages, tracking symbiont communities in replicate fragments of the same colony. Some species' symbionts shifted predictably (heat generally cut symbiont diversity and restructured it), others diverged stochastically, so they frame the responses as a continuum of host-driven symbiont sorting.

title: From Shape to Species: The Use of Persistent Homology in Restructuring the Taxonomy of Acropora corals
digest_headline: Telling Acropora apart by the shape of the data (arXiv preprint, 5 Nov)
summary: Eringfeld, Raynor, Bokor Bleile & Bridge test topological data analysis (persistent homology) on in-situ coral photos as a way to separate species in the notoriously tricky genus Acropora, where molecular evidence keeps outrunning morphology. A first exploration: they show usable topological features can be pulled from field images, not a working classifier yet.

title: Automatically identifying, counting, and describing wild animals in camera-trap images with deep learning
digest_headline: Automatically identifying, counting, and describing wild animals in camera-trap images with deep learning
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Deep CNNs trained on the 3.2-million-image Snapshot Serengeti set identified 48 species with >93.8% accuracy and also counted animals and described behaviours. The clever bit: by only auto-labelling images the network was confident about, it handled 99.3% of the data at the same 96.6% accuracy as the crowdsourced volunteers, saving an estimated 8+ years of human labelling.
caveats: One savanna dataset with plenty of labels per common species; rare species and new sites are much harder, which the later literature hammered home.
since_then: Beery, Morris & Yang's MegaDetector pipeline (2019) split the job into a generic “animal / person / vehicle” detector plus local classifiers, and became the go-to camera-trap tool. arXiv:1907.06772 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.06772)
venue_clean: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

title: Machine learning algorithms to infer trait‐matching and predict species interactions in ecological networks
digest_headline: Machine learning algorithms to infer trait-matching and predict species interactions in ecological networks
summary: Do species interact because their traits match (a bee's tongue and a flower's shape)? Studies disagreed, and the authors argue part of the reason was overly simple GLMs.
caveats: Pollination networks with good trait data; how well this carries over to reef networks with patchy traits and detection bias is open.
since_then: Strydom et al. (2021) laid out a roadmap for predicting interaction networks across space and time, with a small neural-net proof of concept and a methods primer. doi:10.1098/rstb.2021.0063 (https://doi.org/10.1098/rstb.2021.0063)

title: Computational bioacoustics with deep learning: a review and roadmap
digest_headline: Computational bioacoustics with deep learning: a review and roadmap
summary: A single-author tour of deep learning for animal sound: which ideas were borrowed from speech and image processing, where bioacoustic data are genuinely different (rare calls, overlapping sources, shifting backgrounds), and a principled roadmap of open problems the community should tackle. Why it mattered: it's the review people hand to new PAM students, and it set the agenda (low-resource species, generalisation, richer tasks than presence/absence).
caveats: A narrative review with a self-described “subjective but principled” roadmap, written before the foundation-model wave.
since_then: Ghani, Denton, Kahl & Klinck (2023) showed embeddings from large birdsong models transfer to bats, marine mammals and amphibians better than general-audio embeddings, answering one of the roadmap's questions. doi:10.1038/s41598-023-49989-z (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-49989-z)
code_data: Perch (Google Research bioacoustics models and tools) (https://github.com/google-research/perch)

title: Acoustic enrichment can enhance fish community development on degraded coral reef habitat
digest_headline: Acoustic enrichment can enhance fish community development on degraded coral reef habitat
summary: A six-week field experiment: coral-rubble patch reefs with loudspeakers playing healthy-reef sound versus unmanipulated controls. Acoustically enriched patches roughly doubled overall fish abundance and had 50% more species, across all major trophic guilds.
caveats: Small patch reefs over six weeks; attracting fish isn't the same as long-term recovery, and the authors pitch it as a complement to habitat restoration, not a replacement.
since_then: Williams et al. (2022) moved from listening to classifying: ML across a suite of ecoacoustic indices separated healthy and degraded sites at a large reef restoration programme far better than any single index. doi:10.1016/j.ecolind.2022.108986 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolind.2022.108986)

title: Perspectives in machine learning for wildlife conservation
digest_headline: Perspectives in machine learning for wildlife conservation
summary: An 18-author perspective from ecologists and CV researchers: cheap sensors now produce more data than ecologists can process, and the way forward is ML combined with domain knowledge, feeding better inputs into ecological models and, eventually, hybrid ML–ecology models. It also argues for close interdisciplinary teams and training a new generation of ecology data scientists.
caveats: A perspective, not new results; the examples skew terrestrial and the field has since moved fast towards foundation models.
since_then: BioCLIP (Stevens et al., CVPR 2024) trained a vision foundation model on the TreeOfLife-10M dataset, an early step towards the general-purpose biology models the perspective anticipated. arXiv:2311.18803 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.18803)

title: MICE: Multi-animal Interaction Context Encoder - A Hierarchical Foundation Model for Mouse Behavior
digest_headline: MICE: a behaviour foundation model that encodes every animal in the group, and the group itself
summary: Most self-supervised pose models encode each animal separately, so the interaction signal (who approached, chased or groomed whom) gets thrown away. They also hard-code how many animals are in view.
caveats: Lab mice in arenas, with pose already extracted. The authors say the architecture makes no mouse-specific assumptions, but that's untested on other species. Interactions here are within one species (aggression, courtship, allogrooming), not predator–prey or cleaning. A preprint.

title: Anemonefish prioritize mutualistic partner over social group during a marine heatwave
digest_headline: Clownfish stick with their anemone in a heatwave, but squabble more with each other (R Soc Open Sci, 11 Nov)
summary: Noble … Rueger scored video of Amphiprion percula during a marine heatwave in Kimbe Bay, Papua New Guinea. Some host anemones bleached and some didn't, so heat stress could be separated from the indirect effect of a stressed partner.

title: ct: An R package for camera trap data management and multi‐method ecological analysis
digest_headline: ct: a camera-trap R package with an interspecific “encounter response” model (Methods Ecol Evol, 12 Nov)
summary: Gandaho & Palencia take a camera-trap study from raw metadata to inference in one tidy structure, with six density estimators for unmarked populations behind one interface. Of most interest to you: an encounter response model that detects directed short-term changes in one species' detection rate after another species passes.

title: Photogrammetric 3D Model-Based Animal Behavior Classification
digest_headline: Reconstruct the 3D animal first, classify behaviour second (arXiv, 13 Nov)
summary: Hellwich and colleagues argue against end-to-end video-to-behaviour models: video is a 2D projection, so inferring behaviour from it is an ill-posed inverse problem. Their two-stage alternative reconstructs body and object geometry with deformable body priors, then classifies.

title: Cat Royale Comprehensive Dataset: A Dataset for Pose Detection, Segmentation, Animal Action Recognition and Scene Understanding
digest_headline: Cat Royale: segmentation, pose, actions and text captions on the same videos (arXiv, 11 Nov)
summary: Hartley, Ho, Chamberlain, Pound & Benford built it from 500+ hours of video from the Cat Royale art-and-research project: 20,000 images with instance masks, 5,000 with multi-subject pose, 800+ action clips and 800+ clips with text descriptions, with benchmarks for each task. Cats, not corals, but linked annotation types like this are rare and exactly what multimodal behaviour models need. arXiv:2611.15601

title: eDNA metabarcoding and random forest identify super-connector fish species across mangrove–seagrass–coral reef continuums in the South China Sea
digest_headline: eDNA plus random forests find three “super-connector” fish across mangrove, seagrass and reef (Front Ecol Evol, 9 Nov)
summary: Liu … Wang sampled a continuum on Hainan Island and detected 234 fish species, about four times the 58 found by gillnets. Of 23 connector species, three (Lutjanus russellii, Siganus fuscescens, Gerres oyena) carried 47% of cross-habitat network flow, and simulated removal cut connectivity by 68%.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing for marine mammal monitoring
digest_headline: Your seabed cable is a hydrophone array: distributed acoustic sensing for whales (Methods Ecol Evol, 9 Nov)
summary: Bouffaut reviews DAS, which turns existing telecom and energy fibre-optic cables into dense listening arrays read from shore. It can already detect and localise blue and fin whale calls in near-real time.

title: The evolutionary structure of acoustic learnability: a deep learning approach to neotropical birdsong
digest_headline: Which birds are hard for a CNN? Mostly not the ones traits predict (R Soc Open Sci, 11 Nov)
summary: Cortés-Parra, Hortúa & Ríos-Orjuela trained CNNs on 667 Neotropical species (EfficientNetV2L: 94.48% accuracy, macro-F1 94.30%), then asked what explains per-species F1 under phylogenetic control. Broad traits explained about 2.2% of the variance, geographic range size had the most consistent (negative) link, and confusions clustered among close relatives.

title: Global opportunities for climate-resilient coral reef conservation to 2050
digest_headline: Which 30% of reefs to protect? ML maps of reefs most likely to persist to 2050
summary: The authors trained machine-learning ensembles on 45,064 coral field observations (1960–2025) and 42 climate, biophysical and human-pressure predictors to estimate coral cover and community composition in 2020 and 2050. In each ecoregion they then picked the 30% of reef area (the GBF 30x30 target) that jointly maximised current and future cover, composition, spatial cohesion and model certainty.
caveats: The authors are refreshingly upfront: predictive skill was modest and varied among provinces, so these are candidate locations, not definitive priorities, to combine with local knowledge and better monitoring. The fourfold spread between habitat layers shows how much the answer depends on the base map.

title: An autonomous imaging system for reef fish monitoring in the southern Gulf of Mexico
digest_headline: Trail cameras in housings plus RF-DETR give daily reef fish data (Front Mar Sci, 12 Nov)
summary: Guerra-Castro … Simões deployed five adapted trail cameras on Bajo de Diez reef (southern Gulf of Mexico) in 2024 and 2025: 191,758 usable images at 3-min intervals, with 27,471 expert-annotated. RF-DETR reached mAP@50 = 0.741, and its temporal community structure correlated with the experts' (ρ = 0.63), stretching coverage from 68 to 110 dates.

title: Vertical Characteristics of Marine Heatwaves in Global Coral Reef Regions
digest_headline: Deep reefs are no heat refuge: subsurface heatwaves are rarer but stronger (Geophys Res Lett, 10 Nov)
summary: Yao & Wang used two ocean reanalyses (1993–2023): heatwave days decline with depth, but cumulative intensity increases. In El Niño years and the 2020–2023 triple-dip La Niña, intensities reached up to 160 °C-days at 90–150 m.

title: Steroid hormones produced by coral-associated Endozoicomonas influence coral immune response during thermal stress
digest_headline: ICYMI: coral bacteria make steroid hormones that tune the coral immune response in heat (Nature Microbiology, 22 Oct)
summary: Mohamed … Amin found that Endozoicomonas can convert cholesterol into testosterone and progesterone, and that giving corals these hormones during lab heat stress reprogrammed their innate immune response. It's a symbiosis written in chemistry, not behaviour, but still a species interaction. doi:10.1038/s41564-026-02494-1

title: The Target Is a Predicate: Predicate-State Grounding for Semantic-Level Video Reasoning Segmentation
digest_headline: “The target is a predicate”: segment whoever is doing the thing, only while they're doing it (arXiv, 10 Nov)
summary: Hong … Yang define queries as predicates over objects and time (think “the fish currently being cleaned”), so the target can be absent or switch identity. Their PS-Bench has 2,077 videos and 16,250 queries with active/vacant intervals and masks, and their State-Bind-Emit pipeline prompts SAM2 only during active states: +9.32 J&F over baselines and far fewer false masks.

title: What Factors Matter for Collection-Level Counting with Human-AI Collaboration?
digest_headline: Counting with a human in the loop: what actually matters (arXiv, 10 Nov)
summary: Jeong … Sheldon & Maji compare models, estimators and adaptation strategies over 12 counting tasks, from microscopy to aerial wildlife surveys. Off-the-shelf multimodal models are a strong training-free start; fine-tuned detectors win at bigger label budgets; using predictions to choose which images humans check beats uniform sampling.

title: A tabular foundation model rivals established species distribution models from presence-only records
digest_headline: A tabular foundation model matches the best SDM ensemble with zero tuning (bioRxiv, 9 Nov)
summary: Doi, Osawa & Tsutsumida ran TabPFN 3.5 on the standard 225-species benchmark. Untuned, it equalled the best published five-model ensemble (mean AUC 0.732); fine-tuned on other regions it became the best single model (0.736 vs MaxEnt's 0.728) and better calibrated.

title: Pl@ntNet machine-to-machine identification service with Pl@ntNet API: enabling automated biodiversity monitoring through large-scale plant identification
digest_headline: Pl@ntNet's API: 85,000 plant species, no human in the loop (arXiv, 12 Nov)
summary: Bourel … Bonnet describe the machine-to-machine service: species-level accuracy of 0.89, images processed up to 666× faster than human-submitted workflows, and over 84 million requests served. Handy if your camera ever points at a seagrass meadow's terrestrial cousins, or for pollination-network field kits. arXiv:2611.16538

title: Shuck it and see: Adaptive Restoration Engineering in community‐led shellfish reef restoration
digest_headline: “Shuck it and see”: eight years of iterating shellfish-reef restoration structures (Restoration Ecology, 11 Nov)
summary: Porter … Gilchrist assessed 1,081 remnant reef bommies at five Queensland sites and traced how five structure designs (2018–2026) changed as things failed: corroding mesh, burial, subsidence, and mussels recruiting where oysters were expected. The result is “Adaptive Restoration Engineering”: no standard unit, just designs refined for each setting.

title: Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti
digest_headline: Cacti aren't drought-proof: adding severe drought to SDMs sharply raises extinction risk (Nature, 11 Nov)
summary: Pillet … Enquist combined new severe-drought layers with 648,316 occurrence records for 993 cactus species. Drought-aware models were better supported in 91% of cases.

title: pamflow : An open‐source workflow for simplified passive acoustic monitoring data analysis
digest_headline: pamflow: raw recordings to standard outputs with one config file (Methods Ecol Evol, 10 Nov)
summary: Betancourt … Ulloa built an open-source Python/Kedro pipeline with a command-line interface, designed for low budgets and modest hardware. The demo is a participatory project in Colombian Amazonia, where 14 families and a school installed 38 recorders. doi:10.1111/2041-210x.70432

title: Recording session leakage inflates accuracy in marine mammal call classification
digest_headline: Random splits made a whale-call classifier look up to 23 points better than it was
summary: Frey classified 4,761 recordings of nine Arctic and subarctic marine mammal species from the Watkins Marine Mammal Sound Database (recorded on 148 tapes, 1949–1997). Models: a random forest on 90 acoustic features, a small transformer and linear probes on pretrained BirdNET and Perch 2.0 embeddings.
caveats: A single-author preprint on one archival database, where tape and species are tightly confounded (some species sit on only a few tapes), so the size of the gap is probably at the high end. The direction of the effect, though, is well established.

title: Global biodiversity models exhibit low predictive accuracy on local scales
digest_headline: Global biodiversity models infer effects well but predict local sites poorly (Nat Ecol Evol, 10 Nov)
summary: Nyström, Smith, Mandle, Gonzalez, Schön & Andermann find that the mixed models common in biodiversity indicators have low predictive accuracy for local sites, because they lean on highly averaged fixed effects. Swapping study random effects for biome, realm and taxon terms helps, but only modestly, and extrapolating to new contexts stays poor.

title: Which camera-trap images to review? Estimating occupancy from a small part of a survey
digest_headline: Null result for active learning: reviewing the “least certain” camera-trap images first barely beat random (EcoEvoRxiv, 11 Nov)
summary: Tabak simulated partial reviews of four fully labelled surveys (USA, South Africa, Malawi). What worked was confirming one model suggestion per species–site–week.

title: A decade of multi-site acoustic monitoring reveals acoustic co-occurrence of finless porpoises and high-frequency vessel noise
digest_headline: Ten years of porpoise clicks and boat noise: no monotonic decline with noise (Ecol Indicators, 14 Nov)
summary: Ogawa … Akamatsu analysed 2013–2023 PAM data from ten stations in Mikawa Bay, Japan. Porpoises were heard on 99.3% of days and high-frequency vessel noise on 94.8%.

title: COP31 week one: the ocean gets its own ministerial consultations (14 Nov)
digest_headline: COP31 week one: the ocean gets its own ministerial consultations (14 Nov)
summary: As the subsidiary bodies closed in Antalya, the COP31 Presidency set up ministerial consultations on five themes, including the ocean, co-facilitated by Canada (Julie Dabrusin) and Palau (Steven Victor). Whether ocean action makes the final cover decision is still contested.

title: US firms seek seabed-mining exploration licences next to Pacific island states (11 Nov)
digest_headline: US firms seek seabed-mining exploration licences next to Pacific island states (11 Nov)
summary: Two companies applied through the US permitting route, which bypasses the International Seabed Authority, for about 101,000 km² bounded by the Cook Islands, Kiribati and French Polynesia (a fisheries special management area) and about 90,000 km² south of the Cook Islands. French Polynesia has objected.

title: AXOLOTL / AI4OCEAN Winter School, Cyprus, 10–12 Feb 2027: apply by 20 Dec
digest_headline: AXOLOTL / AI4OCEAN Winter School, Cyprus, 10–12 Feb 2027: apply by 20 Dec
summary: Three days on AI-enhanced biodiversity assessment, underwater acoustics, Earth observation and maritime surveillance, with lectures, practicals and field activities, aimed mainly at MSc/PhD students and ECRs. Limited competitive support for registration, travel or accommodation is planned (decisions within 15 days of applying). ai4ocean2027.net

title: Camera Traps, AI & Ecology (Fribourg + online, 21–22 Jan): new abstract-only track due 18 Dec
digest_headline: Camera Traps, AI & Ecology (Fribourg + online, 21–22 Jan): new abstract-only track due 18 Dec

title: Cross‐validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure
digest_headline: Cross-validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure
summary: Reviewing the ecological literature, with simulations and case studies, the authors show that ignoring dependence (in space, time, groups or phylogeny) when cross-validating seriously underestimates predictive error and lets non-causal predictors look useful. Block cross-validation was nearly always more appropriate than random CV when the goal is predicting to new data.
caveats: Mostly SDM-style regression examples; choosing block size and blocking variable is still a judgement call.
since_then: Ploton et al. (2020) showed the stakes: a forest-biomass model that looked like it explained over half the variation under random validation had quasi-null predictive power under spatial validation. doi:10.1038/s41467-020-18321-y (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-18321-y)

title: Recognition in Terra Incognita
digest_headline: Recognition in Terra Incognita
summary: Images from 20 camera traps, with a simple challenge: train at a handful of locations, then detect and classify animals at new locations with no training data. State-of-the-art models did very well at the cameras they were trained on, but generalised poorly to new ones, especially for classification. Camera traps are fixed, so the background barely changes, and models learn it.
caveats: Small by today's standards (20 cameras, American Southwest), and CNNs from 2018. Modern foundation models narrow the gap but don't close it.
since_then: Beery et al.'s Context R-CNN (2020) turned the fixed background into an asset, using a per-camera memory of unlabelled frames to boost detection at new cameras. arXiv:1912.03538 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.03538)
interest_area: Transferable CV/ML: camera traps and domain shift

title: WILDS: A Benchmark of in-the-Wild Distribution Shifts
digest_headline: WILDS: A Benchmark of in-the-Wild Distribution Shifts
summary: The ML community took the hint. WILDS curated 10 datasets with real distribution shifts, including shifts across camera traps for wildlife monitoring (iWildCam), across hospitals and across time and place in satellite imagery. On every dataset, standard training gave substantially lower out-of-distribution than in-distribution performance, and existing robustness methods didn't close the gap.
caveats: Benchmarks fix the shift in advance; your deployment shift (new reef, new season, new turbidity) may look nothing like theirs.
since_then: WILDS 2.0 (Sagawa et al., ICLR 2022) added curated unlabelled data to 8 of the 10 datasets to test whether unlabelled deployment data can mitigate shift. arXiv:2112.05090 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.05090)

title: Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science
digest_headline: Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science
summary: Zooming out from ecology: a literature survey found leakage in 17 fields, affecting 294 papers, sometimes leading to wildly overoptimistic conclusions. The authors give a taxonomy of eight types of leakage, from textbook errors to open problems, and propose “model info sheets” to check for each. In a civil-war prediction case study, once errors were fixed, complex ML models did no better than decades-old logistic regression.
caveats: It mostly covers social and biomedical fields; ecology appears only lightly, so the ecological examples are up to you.
since_then: Kapoor et al. (2024) turned it into REFORMS, a consensus 32-question checklist for ML-based science from 19 researchers across disciplines. doi:10.1126/sciadv.adk3452 (https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adk3452)

title: Global birdsong embeddings enable superior transfer learning for bioacoustic classification
digest_headline: Global birdsong embeddings enable superior transfer learning for bioacoustic classification
summary: The constructive ending. Instead of training from scratch on scarce labels, the authors used feature embeddings from large audio classifiers to learn new classes from a few examples: bird call types and dialects, bats, marine mammals and amphibians. Embeddings from models trained on bird vocalisations consistently beat those trained on general audio, even for non-bird taxa.
caveats: Transfer quality still varies by taxon and dataset, and few-shot results are only as honest as the split they're scored on (see above).
since_then: van Merriënboer et al. (2024) reviewed how to evaluate such bioacoustic foundation models fairly, given the noise, class imbalance and distribution shifts typical of PAM. doi:10.3389/fbirs.2024.1369756 (https://doi.org/10.3389/fbirs.2024.1369756)
